subject: BlueOrbit connector: uptime impact, immediate remediation and partner SLA discussion
messages:
From: BlueOrbit Support <support@blueorbit.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, eng-ops@blueorbit.com
Cc: linda@blueorbit.com
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: connector timeouts seen from BlueOrbit -> Redwood (possible SLA impact)

Hi Monica,

We started seeing recurring 504 timeouts from the Redwood connector in our staging and a handful of production customers since ~14:30 PDT. Error rates spike when payloads exceed ~120KB and the connector appears to stall for ~30-45s before failing. This is causing downstream delivery retries and two of our customers flagged it as a live-issue.

Attached is a log bundle and a short trace (connector-logs-20260910.tar.gz). We also included a sample failing request in the bundle.

Can your team confirm whether this maps to any recent routing or kernel selection changes? If this is a platform-side regression, we need an ETA on a mitigation path and any suggested temporary operational workarounds (e.g., request size trimming, alternate endpoint). BlueOrbit treats >99.9% uptime for connector webhooks as part of our partner commitments and we want to escalate proactively.

Thanks,
Linda Park
Partner Engineering
BlueOrbit Consulting

--
Attachment: connector-logs-20260910.tar.gz (log bundle, 2.4MB)

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: BlueOrbit Support <support@blueorbit.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: connector timeouts seen from BlueOrbit -> Redwood (possible SLA impact)

Hi Linda — thanks for the quick flag and the logs. I'm escalating this to our support lead and Partner Ops so we can coordinate a live triage.

Rishi / Marissa — can you pick this up as P1? Initial asks:
- Immediate health check on the connector fleet routing that handles BlueOrbit (trace IDs in logs look related to cluster eu-west-1/rdw-psi).
- Can we enable a temporary fallback route to a lower-latency pool while we investigate?
- I attached a short diagnostics request — please populate and return so we get consistent traces (redwood-diagnostics-request.pdf).

Linda — please confirm whether the failing payloads are trimmed in your stack or if the full JSON arrives at our endpoint. Any sample payloads are helpful. We'll stand up a 30-min triage call if that helps.

I will coordinate communication cadence with your team; want to avoid surprise customer-facing incidents.

—Monica
Director, Partner Success
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: redwood-diagnostics-request.pdf (PDF, 14KB)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, BlueOrbit Support <support@blueorbit.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: connector timeouts seen from BlueOrbit -> Redwood (possible SLA impact)

On Thu, Sep 10, 2026 at 15:28, monica_patel@redwood.ai wrote:
> Monica — thanks for the quick flag and the logs. I'm escalating this to our support lead and Partner Ops so we can coordinate a live triage.

Thanks Monica. Hi Linda — I’m taking point for operational triage. Quick notes from initial log inspection: several requests are hitting our inference runtime queue but then time out during KV-cache retrieval; queuing latency spikes correlate with specific sequence lengths and larger payloads.

Immediate actions we will take in parallel:
1) Launch a short live triage (15–30m) — I propose 15:55 PDT today. Please confirm availability.
2) Flip a routing knob to route BlueOrbit traffic to a smaller, low-concurrency pool (reduces batching pressure) — this is non-disruptive but may increase per-token cost temporarily.
3) Gather a sample failing payload (payload-sample.json) from your side and we’ll run it through a local repro.

If this indicates a regression we will classify as P1 and keep you updated every 30 minutes. If it looks like a payload-shape/size issue, we'll propose a partner-level mitigation (payload batching/streaming guidance) and a short-term SLA credit calculation template for finance.

Sharing screen on the triage call is helpful. If we need to extend beyond 30m we’ll escalate into our on-call.

From: BlueOrbit EngOps <eng-ops@blueorbit.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Linda Park <linda@blueorbit.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: connector timeouts seen from BlueOrbit -> Redwood (possible SLA impact)

Rishi — we ran a quick capture and the failing requests all contain a new analytics array that pushed the request over ~120KB. The sample is attached (payload-sample.json). We can try payload trimming but the analytics data is required for a subset of our customers, so trimming is only a short-term workaround.

Preliminary root cause: our SDK started embedding full-session analytics in the webhook JSON last night as part of a rollout. We missed a size regression test in the SDK pipeline.

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood confirm whether a 45s timeout is platform behavior or if this is a config value we can tweak on the connector side? We need explicit confirmation for our customers when we tell them about the incident and any credit requests.
- If this counts as a platform incident, what is Redwood’s SLA credit policy threshold and how do we file a credit request?

We can join a follow-up call this morning if you want to walk through the sample.

Thanks —
Alex (on behalf of BlueOrbit EngOps)

--
Attachment: payload-sample.json (4.8KB)

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: BlueOrbit Support <support@blueorbit.com>, BlueOrbit EngOps <eng-ops@blueorbit.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, finance-billing@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: connector timeouts seen from BlueOrbit -> Redwood (possible SLA impact)

Alex / Linda — thanks for the root-cause confirmation and the sample payload. Summary and next steps from Redwood: 

1) Immediate operational mitigation (completed): we enabled a low-concurrency fallback pool for BlueOrbit traffic at 16:10 PDT on 2026-09-10. This reduced tail latencies and the error-rate dropped to baseline for the impacted customers.

2) Platform behavior vs config: the 45s behavior you observed is a combination of our default request read timeout and a runtime-level KV-cache retrieval retry window. We can surface and tune the connector read timeout as a per-partner config; I’ve asked Engineering (Rishi) to validate safe bounds and a documented knob.

3) Classification & SLA credits: we will treat the customer-impacting regression as a partner-impact incident and begin formal incident review. Our finance team needs the timeline and customer list to assess credits — I’ve CC’d finance-billing. For BlueOrbit, we’ll start with a goodwill credit proposal (covers measured downtime windows where requests routinely failed) while we finalize formal credit terms under the partner MOU.

4) Remediation & prevention: Engineering will add a size-regression check to partner SDK gating and we will publish guidance on payload streaming and chunking. We’ll also add an alert on sequence-length distributions for partner routes.

5) Ask of BlueOrbit: please confirm the customers impacted and whether the analytics payload is required for all production customers or a subset. Also sign the short MOU that defines SLA credit windows and operational responsibilities — link: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/BlueOrbit/mou-draft-20260912 (editable doc).

Proposed follow-ups:
- 24h postmortem draft by 2026-09-13 18:00 PDT (owner: Rishi).
- Joint SDK gating plan and rollout window during week of Sep 20.
- Finance and partner ops will sync to finalize credit figure by Sep 17.

We’ll keep the lines open and I’ll coordinate the postmortem. Thanks for working through this quickly.

—Monica Patel
Director, Partner Success | Redwood Inference
